conviction_note: I found a mild positive lean and nothing decisive. A peer's litter category grew, the June 24 price-increase notice likely pulled July orders forward, and the Oct 7 refinancing removed the acquisition cap. Against that, the company itself flagged margin and freight pressure and drew down its backlog in Q3. The findings sum to +0.8. The scaled number is +0.9 (p_up 55 x abs 9.0). The guided floor (FY net income above $54.0m) is public and sits under the likely print, so the stock trades on how far above the floor it lands and on the FY27 tone, and that is a coin with a slight tilt.
bar: Company guide: the CEO said in the Q3 release 'we expect to achieve our annual plan and surpass last year's net income'. FY25 net income was $53.996m and 9M FY26 net income was $42.551m, so the implied Q4 floor is net income above about $11.45m, roughly $0.79 diluted EPS. Prior-year Q4 was $13.0m and $0.89 on $125.2m of sales. Sources: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000074046/000162828026041544/odcf26q3ex991-earningsrele.htm and https://finviz.com/news/188665/oil-dri-delivers-strongest-annual-financial-results-in-history-bolstered-by-solid-fourth-quarter-performance. I found no sell-side consensus (Yahoo shows '--' everywhere, Seeking Alpha is paywalled). print_vs_bar is my estimate of Q4 net income of about $12.1m against the $11.45m floor.
positioning_check: 404.7K shares short with 3.37 days to cover at the 2026-07-15 settlement, up from 372.4K on 06-30 and from a 310.5K low on 05-15 (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/odc/short-interest/). Equibles shows an undated 2.60% of float and 3.8 days. I found no September settlement. This is not a crowded short. There is no options market, so no skew. Tape: spot 85.56, -6.4% over 5 days, -0.74% over 20 days, 19.6% below the 52-week high (about $106-107 after the post-Q3 spike). Sealed spot was struck at 13:09 ET on Oct 8.

findings.finding: Church & Dwight said Arm & Hammer cat litter consumption rose 7.5% in Apr-Jun 2026 and share rose 0.8pt to 24.5%, which implies US litter category growth of about 4% over two of ODC's three Q4 months (May-Jul). Clorox's Fresh Step is still in turnaround, and ODC's Q3 domestic litter ex co-pack was +10% with co-pack +94%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Retail & Wholesale (litter) drove the record Q3 of 2026-06-08, which went +17.38%. A weak first half against a tough comparison went -12.55% on 2025-12-08.
findings.why_not_priced: ODC has no sell-side estimate to update on peer data, and the stock fell 6.4% in the five sessions into the print. If a strong-category read-through were priced, the stock would sit nearer the post-Q3 level of about $100 than at 85.56. It is a peer's number, though, so it is only partly unpriced.
findings.independence: This is a proxy. ODC's own Q3 release (a different document) reported domestic litter +10% ex co-pack and record crystal litter: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000074046/000162828026041544/odcf26q3ex991-earningsrele.htm. Management also cited 'elevated promotional activity' on the Q3 call, which cuts against it and is netted into the size.

findings.finding: On 2026-06-24 ODC announced price increases on most products effective in Q1 FY27 (Aug-Oct), citing freight, resin packaging and health insurance. A notice five weeks before Q4 ended plausibly pulled customer orders into July, inside Q4, and it sets up FY27 margin recovery for the outlook commentary.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock rose 1.75% on 2026-06-25 when the increase was announced. Prior pricing actions (domestic industrial +3% in Q3) were part of the record Q3 that went +17.38%.
findings.why_not_priced: The notice is public, but the pre-buy effect on Q4 volumes is an inference that no estimate carries, and there is no consensus to raise. If it were priced, the stock would not have drifted from about $102 in June to 85.56.
findings.independence: This is an inference and I found no document confirming a pre-buy. Company release mirror: https://www.barchart.com/story/news/2634393/oil-dri-announces-price-increases-to-address-higher-external-costs (same announcement, so not independent).

findings.finding: Margin pressure into Q4. Q3 domestic COGS per ton was +6%, gross margin fell 190bp to 26.7%, and freight was still rising. Q3 SG&A was flattered by $2.5m from a lower bonus accrual. The CEO said 'margins are going to continue to get pressured' and flagged transportation and input-cost headwinds against the plan. Q4 FY25 gross margin was 27.8% and had a low tax rate.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin compression on a tough comparison went -12.55% on 2025-12-08. Q3 gross margin fell 190bp but net income beat and the stock went +17.38%, so this name has paid on net income rather than gross margin.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: management said it on the call and the stock is 19.6% off its high. What is not priced is the bonus-accrual reversal and the size of any Q4 freight spike. The company's guided floor already allows for headwinds, so this lands mostly inside the guide.
findings.independence: The Q3 release (separate document) shows COGS/ton +6% and the lower bonus accrual: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000074046/000162828026041544/odcf26q3ex991-earningsrele.htm

findings.finding: 8-K accepted 2026-10-07 20:02 ET. ODC raised its BMO revolver from $75m to $100m to 2031, set the accordion at the greater of $125m or 100% of EBITDA, raised the PGIM shelf from $75m to $150m, cut pricing, and removed the $100m cumulative permitted-acquisitions cap, adding a restricted-payments covenant. Cash is rising ($62.9m at Q3) and leverage is low, so this buys M&A capacity rather than signalling distress. The CEO also called the fiscal year-end 'exciting' on the Q3 call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no print-day precedent. The Ultra Pet acquisition ($46m, 2024) was funded the same way through the revolver and a PGIM Series D note and was accretive to litter sales.
findings.why_not_priced: It was filed after the close the night before. Through the 13:09 ET seal on Oct 8 the stock had no visible reaction (it is down 6.4% over 5 days), and a covenant 8-K on a name with no coverage gets no wire copy. If the market read it as a deal precursor, the stock would be bid into the print.
findings.independence: Q3 call 'exciting' year-end remark (different document): https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2916921. I found no announced 2026 acquisition, so the use of the money is not corroborated.

findings.finding: Fluids purification and B2B read-through. US renewable diesel output hit records in May and June 2026 (June biomass-based diesel 494m gallons, renewable diesel 327m), and the Q3 call cited strong refinery margins, jet-fuel mineral-oil purification and new SAF capacity.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: B2B has not been the line the stock trades on. Q3 B2B was +3% with fluids purification -1% inside a +17.38% day.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a macro-to-company link that no estimate tracks. It is sized small because ODC's own Q3 fluids purification fell 1% while April renewable diesel output was already high, which weakens the transmission.
findings.independence: Q3 call (Bruce Pacey on refinery margins and SAF): https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2916921. The ODC Q3 release shows fluids purification -1%, which argues against the link and is netted into the size.

findings.finding: Backlog fell $2.2m during Q3, which the company says shifted revenue recognition into Q3. Q4 therefore started with less backlog, a small drag on Q4 sales of about 1.8% of a $125m quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Order-timing shifts were part of the 2025-12-08 miss (-12.55%) and of the record Q3 (+17.38%).
findings.why_not_priced: It is in the release but has no wire coverage, and no estimate carries a Q4 sales number to cut. It is small, and management's floor already accounts for it.
findings.independence: The same document is the source for finding 3's SG&A detail, which is a different line. Winter Storm Fern timing on the Q3 call: https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2916921

rejected_candidates.candidate: The Q4 guide floor (FY net income above FY25's $54.0m) treated as a positive finding
rejected_candidates.detail: It is the bar the findings are sized against (see 'bar'), so filing it again as a finding would count the same document twice.
EIA/FRED monthly Henry Hub of $2.77-3.15 for Apr-Jun 2026 is not above the prior year, and the Q3 call never mentioned gas, so the sweep's premise did not hold.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. A mild long cuts slightly against the -6.4% 5-day drift, but on a name 19.6% off its high with a guided floor under the print, the drift reads as a lower bar rather than priced disappointment.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (proxy loses to the company number): A&H category read-through cut from +1.0 to +0.8, and renewable diesel cut from +0.4 to +0.2 because ODC's own Q3 fluids purification (-1%) argues against the transmission.
Lessons 5 and 6 (inference; inside what the company guided): price-increase pre-buy cut from +0.8 to +0.5 as an unconfirmed inference.
Lesson 6 (inside the guide): the margin-pressure negative shrank from -1.2 to -0.9 because the CEO's floor already allows for transportation and input-cost headwinds.

Lesson 4 (financing is a question): kept positive after asking what it buys (acquisition capacity, low leverage, rising cash, no distress), but cut from +0.8 to +0.6 because the use is not corroborated by any announced deal.
Lesson 8 (thin coverage moves more): abs_move_pct raised from 8.0 to 9.0 on a no-consensus, no-options name whose last beat went +17.4%. p_up moved from 56 to 55 for the proxy weight.
Lessons 1 and 7 left standing: beats have been bought here (+17.38%, +8.23%), so the reaction function does not veto a mild long, and short interest of 3.4 days is not crowded.
